task.title: Decompose the Workshop backend and consolidate Agora persistence

root_cause.summary: services/control-plane/bff/agora/strategy_workshop/router.py was a single 4073-line create_strategy_workshop_router() factory: 18 route handlers, a ~900-line command-admission/compensation helper cluster, a readiness-assessment builder, a card-projection builder, an SSE pub/sub implementation, and eight Pydantic request models all defined as one closure. Two of the module-level SSE/readiness helpers (_ws_publish, _build_readiness_assessment) were leading-underscore (router-private) names imported directly by agora/interaction/runner.py, agora/research/router.py, and agora/trading_room/router.py -- a private-by-name, public-by-usage contract with no owning module.
candidates_ruled_out: Duplicating the admission/compensation helper cluster into each of the four new route-group files: rejected because it would create four independent, divergent copies of the ETag/idempotency/CAS command lifecycle and compensation logic -- exactly the kind of duplicate-truth surface the cleanup program forbids (no_new_facade_or_truth_store).

Leaving _ws_publish and _build_readiness_assessment as router-private names and updating only the docstring: rejected because the acceptance criterion is a structural one (a public module each caller can import), not a naming convention.
root_cause.confirmed_cause: The Workshop router grew one route at a time inside a single factory closure with no internal module boundaries, so cross-router callers had no public surface to import from and reached into router.py's leading-underscore internals via lazy imports instead.

changes: Added strategy_workshop/events.py: the public Workshop SSE pub/sub module (moved verbatim from router.py's module-level _ws_* functions and _workshop_sse_buffers/_workshop_sse_subscribers state). agora/interaction/runner.py and agora/research/router.py now import _ws_publish from strategy_workshop.events instead of strategy_workshop.router (ACG-06-002).

Added strategy_workshop/readiness.py: the public readiness-assessment module, exposing build_readiness_assessment as its stable public entry point (moved verbatim from router.py's _build_readiness_assessment and its exclusive helper cluster) (ACG-06-003).

Added strategy_workshop/cards.py: the live-card projection helpers (_build_workshop_cards, _merge_cards, and their dependents), split out so both router.py and routes/session.py can import one implementation without a circular import.
Added strategy_workshop/schemas.py: the eight Workshop request Pydantic models, moved out of router.py so the route-group modules can import them without importing router.py back.

Added strategy_workshop/_admission.py: build_admission_context(), wrapping the ~900-line command-admission/compensation closure cluster (ETag parsing, idempotency-key admission, CAS completion, resume/compensation, MFA-gated approval) verbatim out of the old factory body. One router assembly builds exactly one context and hands it to all four route groups, so there is exactly one implementation of the command lifecycle (ACG-06-004).

Added strategy_workshop/routes/{session,versions,execution,stream}.py: the 18 route handlers split into four disjoint groups -- session (11: list/create/read/message/events/completeness/cards/readiness/reconstruct), versions (3: list/create/select), execution (3: research-runs/consultations/conclude), stream (1: SSE aggregate) -- each a build_*_router(...) factory taking the shared store/canonical/admission-context and returning its own APIRouter. Route bodies are unchanged from the original implementation.

Rewrote strategy_workshop/router.py (4073 -> 163 lines) as composition-only: it builds the store/canonical-operations/private-content-store, builds one admission context, and flattens the four subrouters' already-built route objects onto one APIRouter.routes list (chosen over router.include_router() -- see 'router.include_router lazy-wrapping' below). It keeps back-compat re-exports (with # noqa: F401) for every previously-importable name (_ws_publish, _build_readiness_assessment, _StrategyVersionProjectionError, the Workshop*Request models, etc.) so no external test file needed to change its import path.

Added tests/test_agora_route_ownership.py: asserts the 18 contracts are registered exactly once and are disjoint across the four route-group modules, that interaction/runner.py and research/router.py no longer import a leading-underscore name from strategy_workshop.router, that readiness/events expose a public entry point, and that MemoryWorkshopStore is only ever used via explicit injection into the router factory.
fix.not_changing: agora/router.py needed no changes -- create_strategy_workshop_router()'s public signature is unchanged, so its single call site continues to work unmodified. agora/trading_room/router.py's two lazy `from ..strategy_workshop.router import _build_readiness_assessment` imports are left as-is: trading_room/router.py is outside this task's declared artifact_conflict_guard.artifact_scope, and router.py's back-compat re-export keeps that import working byte-for-byte, so nothing there needed to change to stay correct. strategy_workshop/store.py, operations.py, reconstruction.py, and runner.py are unmodified -- ACG-06-005/006/007 (PostgresStrategyWorkshopStore bootstrap-class merge, and the MemoryWorkshopStore-implicit-default in make_workshop_store()) are deliberately deferred; see scope_deferral below. main.py and read_store.py (ACG-01-010, ACG-02-009, ACG-02-010's generic Agora signal/journal/legacy-method duplicates) are outside this task's declared artifact scope entirely and are untouched.
fix.owned_layer: The strategy_workshop router's internal module decomposition and the two cross-router import sites this task owns (interaction/runner.py, research/router.py). Not owned: agora/trading_room/router.py's parallel import site, strategy_workshop/store.py's backend-selection defaults, and main.py/read_store.py's unrelated generic-route duplicates.

scope_deferral.note: ACG-06-006 (MERGE PostgresStrategyWorkshopStore's three bootstrap methods into PostgresWorkshopStore, then delete the class) and the store-selection half of ACG-06-005/ACG-06-007 (make_workshop_store() defaults to MemoryWorkshopStore when AGORA_WORKSHOP_STORE_BACKEND is unset, and scripts/run_agora_interaction_worker.py -- outside this task's artifact scope -- has its own Memory fallback) are deliberately deferred out of this task. PostgresStrategyWorkshopStore bootstraps a materially different DDL surface than PostgresWorkshopStore's own inline bootstrap (it additionally creates agora_private_content_object, which PostgresWorkshopStore does not) and is exercised only by tests/test_strategy_workshop_store_bootstrap.py's frozen five-table deep-closure contract assertions -- confirmed via repo-wide grep that no production code path constructs it. Merging the two without first resolving whether agora_private_content_object is live-required in PostgresWorkshopStore's own schema risks silently changing production Postgres bootstrap DDL, which this task's own acceptance array does not require (it only requires PostgresWorkshopStore be the sole store PostgresStrategyWorkshopStore is not a production caller of either way) and which the architecture_cleanup_rules.move_and_delete_same_delivery_unit rule would require resolving correctly in one delivery, not partially. Likewise, changing make_workshop_store()'s documented 'off -> memory, safe for dev and tests' default to fail closed is a live-deployment-environment policy decision (there is no existing signal in this call site distinguishing dev/paper from live) that this router-decomposition task cannot safely make unilaterally. All three are recorded here as follow-up scope for a dedicated ACG-06-BE store-hardening task, not silently dropped.
scope_deferral.router_include_router_lazy_wrapping: The installed fastapi (0.139.2) wraps a router.include_router(child) call in a lazily-resolved _IncludedRouter node on the parent's .routes list; this is transparent to request dispatch and to app.openapi() but breaks several pre-existing tests (test_workshop_stream_ag_be_sw_004.py, test_agora_workshop_live_operations.py) that walk router.routes directly for a route's .path/.endpoint, since that pattern predates this task and previously worked because the single-file factory never called include_router internally. Fixed by extending router.routes with each subrouter's already-built route objects instead of calling include_router, which reproduces the exact flat route list the single-file factory used to produce.
